overview: A regional lull holds: Iran and the US appear to be in a cautious pause rather than active strikes, though the Caspian Sea incident and Iran-Ukraine tensions show how fragile that is. Closer to home, Turkey's economic picture and a NATO deployment dominate practical news, while Washington's asylum overhaul and Montenegro's visa change matter for anyone tracking regional mobility.
title: The Bosphorus Brief — Tuesday, 28 July 2026
sections: [{"heading": "Money: Lira Steady, Inflation Forecasts Rising", "body": "The Central Bank held its policy rate at 37 percent this week, while Deutsche Bank raised its Turkey inflation forecast to 30 percent — a signal that price pressures remain a longer fight than some had hoped. The lira sits at 47.34 to the dollar and 53.92 to the euro; Commerzbank notes tight CBRT funding is offering only marginal support to the currency. Fortune also flags that fuel prices tied to the Iran situation are rippling into daily costs from Turkey to Chile and Nepal — worth watching at the pump and in grocery bills over coming weeks."}, {"heading": "Iran-US Standoff: Cautious Pause, Not Peace", "body": "President Trump said US-Iran talks are underway during a lull in strikes and suggested \"something could happen,\" though Iran denies direct talks are happening. Al Jazeera reports Qatari and Pakistani mediators are working to restart ceasefire talks amid the fragile pause. Separately, Iran struck a vessel in the Caspian Sea it linked to Ukraine, prompting Kyiv to dismiss Tehran's threats and Iran's foreign minister to call the strike something that "cannot go unanswered." For residents in the wider region, this remains a situation to monitor rather than act on — travel advisories for Iran, Iraq, Syria and Lebanon remain at Level 4."}, {"heading": "Turkey's NATO Role and F-35 Politics", "body": "Turkey will send five F-16s and 76 personnel to Estonia from August through November for NATO's Baltic Air Policing mission, operating out of Ämari Air Base — reported via state-run Anadolu and picked up by pro-government outlets. Separately, Trump was asked about F-35 sales to Turkey and pushed back on any suggestion he'd be told what the US can sell, a comment covered across international and Turkish outlets alike, including in response to Israeli objections. No policy change has been announced; this is a rhetorical moment, not a done deal."}, {"heading": "Visas, Asylum, and Legal Security", "body": "Montenegro will end visa-free entry for Russian and Belarusian citizens from November 1, a move tied to its 2028 EU membership bid — relevant for anyone with Balkan travel plans. In the US, a new federal rule shifts hundreds of thousands of asylum cases into immigration courts and strips a prior interview requirement, which advocacy groups say will speed deportations; the Center for Migration Studies separately condemned the ending of TPS protections for Haitians and Syrians. Munich Airport, meanwhile, opened a new Asylum and Border Management Center. Separately, State Department attention to religious freedom conditions in Egypt continues, covered mainly by US outlets."}]
closing: Stay steady, keep an eye on fuel prices, and check visa rules before booking regional travel — see you tomorrow.
